A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, Does equivariance matter at scale? Their complete text, six figures, two tables, equations, and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original rigid-body prediction experiments comparing standard transformers and GATr, including data augmentation, fitted scaling laws, test losses, and throughput measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and results in Sections 3–4, Tables 1–2, Figures 1–6, and the appendices.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same transformer architectures, input embeddings, hierarchical attention, and rigid-object output construction. Table 1 and Appendix B retain the model specifications; added explanations do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same Kubric/MOVi-B-style rigid-body prediction task and data- and compute-scaling scenarios. Appendix A newly describes the ground plane and gravity, without reporting different data or an additional test scenario.

E2.justification: Compute-scaling comparisons retain the standard transformer and GATr. Data-scaling comparisons retain those models plus the augmented standard transformer. No comparator is added or removed from the corresponding experiments.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, loss metric, optimization, architecture families, and compute budgets remain unchanged. v2 specifies the augmentation transformations, which v1 left unspecified; this is additional documentation, not evidence of a revised experiment.

E4.justification: The throughput analysis in Appendix C and preliminary output-parameterization comparisons in Section 3.2 and Appendix B are retained. No new ablation, sensitivity experiment, robustness test, or case study appears.

E5.justification: Both use 10,000 nonparametric bootstrap resamples and report 95% confidence intervals for scaling coefficients and derived predictions. The expanded Figure 1 caption explains uncertainty bands already present in v1.

E6.justification: Table 2 values, Equations (6)–(8), and results plotted in Figures 1–6 match. Compute-loss exponents remain 0.268 for the baseline and 0.236 for GATr, with unchanged performance trends and augmentation findings.

T1.justification: The equivariance definition, scaling-law equations and derivations, and output transformation are retained. Appendix B adds qualitative architectural clarification about parameter subspaces, without introducing a new formal result, assumption, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same three conclusions concerning data efficiency, compute scaling, and optimal model-size/training-duration allocation. The expanded conclusion emphasizes implications already central to v1.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 adds an alternative E(2) interpretation with fixed gravity. Appendix B explains why equivariant architectures generally cannot simply be identified with parameter subspaces of standard architectures. The existing generalization, runtime, and extrapolation limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 specifies manual tuning of depth, width, and attention heads at low/intermediate budgets; augmentation using planar translations and rotations about gravity; and the ground-plane position and gravity direction. These clarify previously underspecified implementation and data details.

R1.justification: The introduction adds contextual citations to Oxford Protein Informatics Group, Joshi, and Twitter/X discussions. Appendix B adds a comparison with steerable CNNs. Most other reference changes update publication metadata for already cited research.

P1.justification: Localized additions explain benchmark motivation, symmetry choices, tuning, and how to read Figure 2. v2 adds a labeled Conclusions paragraph and edits spelling and terminology, while retaining the main section sequence and most prose.

P2.justification: The document adopts TMLR formatting throughout, changing typography, margins, title/author layout, and running headers. Figures are enlarged and redistributed, Figures 1–2 move off the first page, and table captions move above their tables. Scientific display content is retained.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves reproducibility and interpretation by documenting augmentation and tuning more precisely and clarifying the architectural comparison in Appendix B. These address omissions in v1. The empirical evidence, central conclusions, and acknowledged single-benchmark and nominal-FLOP limitations remain unchanged.
